resolved_conflicts.explanation: NRHP text says completed 1873 while its tower heading and the station record say 1875; LighthouseFriends gives 1875 above the door. Story uses 1873 completion and 1875 light.
NRHP dates the $10,000 appropriation to 1872; LighthouseFriends to 1874. Story gives both.
NRHP names Yaquina in one place and Yakima in another; LighthouseFriends says Yaquina Bay Lighthouse. Story gives Yaquina and notes the variant.

notes_for_editor: (1) The 1912 lens: LighthouseFriends says a fourth-order lens replaced the fifth; the NRHP (1991) and the USLHS record say fifth order. Unresolved; the story reports both. (2) The 1872 (NRHP) and 1874 (LighthouseFriends) dates for the $10,000 appropriation, and 1873 (NRHP, citing the 1873 Annual Report, which the corpus does not hold) versus 1874 (LighthouseFriends) for the fog bell, are unresolved. (3) The San Francisco Call OCR reads 'John F. Kofod'; the roster has John P. Kofod. Check the page image before the editor uses the initial. (4) The station record's visit.boat_only is true; no source in this research says that, and the island is reachable by road. Check. (5) The 1873-1876 Light-House Board reports are not in the local corpus; the NRHP is the only source for the early chronology. (6) The fog-signal hours (1900) are from the Light-House Board volume's scan page 215; the printed page was not read off the image. (7) The 1909 fire is from the Call's own report, with LighthouseFriends for the upper rooms. (8) LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts only; the few phrases quoted are short. (9) Chronicling America: 126 hits for 'Yerba Buena' with 'lighthouse' (CA, 1873-1915) were mostly unrelated; the fire was found with 'Kofod fire lighthouse' in 1909. (10) Fact-check 2026-10-22: re-read against the NRHP nomination, LighthouseFriends, the 1912 and 1932 Bulletins (PDF pp. 41 and 6 confirmed by corpus.py page), the 1900 Light-House Board report (scan 215 confirmed), the San Francisco Call of 18 July 1909 p. 21 (headline and the household-goods, Vigilant, hose and alarm passages confirmed in the page text), and the USLHS roster. (11) The Call's OCR reads 'John F. Kofod'; the story says only 'Kofod' for the assistant keeper, and the roster's 'John P. Kofod' is linked to him only through LighthouseFriends' account. (12) The '55 keeper entries' in the story is the count of roster lines roster.py printed, not a figure a page states. (13) LighthouseFriends' quotations in the earlier draft were paraphrased; the one kept is Rhodes's remark, quoted as LighthouseFriends prints it. (14) The record's '1887' remodel of the fog-signal building was corrected to 1886 (LighthouseFriends).
